claims: 4-stroke In the world of engines, the gas/oil ratio is a crucial concept, especially when it comes to 2-stroke (2t) engines.
Unlike 4-stroke engines, which have a separate oil compartment, 2-stroke engines require a mixture of gasoline (petrol) and oil to operate.
This mixture is necessary for a few critical reasons: Lubrication — In 2-stroke engines, the gas and oil mix provides the necessary lubrication for internal parts.
2-stroke engines can run hot, and the oil helps dissipate heat away from critical areas.
Common ratios include 50:1 (50 parts gasoline to 1 part oil) or 40:1.
Check out the mix ratio table below to see how much oil you need to add to your gasoline to attain one of the 5 most popular mix ratios.
How to use our gas oil ratio calculator to find gas and oil mix Our calculator is a user-friendly tool designed to help you mix gas and oil correctly for your 2-stroke engine.
Here’s how to use our gas oil ratio calculator: Set your ratio — The default mixture of gas to oil is 50:1, but you can change it.
A 50 to 1 mixture refers to the ratio of gasoline to oil used in 2-stroke engines.
This means for every 50 parts of gasoline, you mix in 1 part of oil.
